issues.title: Non-positive inner vector dimensions floor vectorElemMinSize to 1, letting bound balloon…
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed by direct test: unmarshalVector on vector<vector<float,-3>,1048576> over a 1MB payload allocates ~25MB (24 bytes/slice-header x 1M claimed dims) before the inner Unmarshal call finally rejects the -3 dimension; vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1125-1145) skips its recursive branch whenever an inner VectorType's Dimensions<=0 and falls through to the 'size<1 return 1' floor, so the outer bound (marshal.go:998-1003) accepts far more dimensions than a correctly-sized element would allow. Also confirmed the inverse: a genuinely valid vector<vector<float,0>,5> over a 0-byte payload is wrongly rejected ('5 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes') because the floor treats the 0-byte inner vector as needing 1 byte. frame.go:861 and helpers.go:264 both parse nested dim via strconv.Atoi with no dim>=1 check, so such types are reachable from the wire today.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize and the dimension bound are wholly new in this PR, and their handling of non-positive nested dimensions is what causes both the amplification and the wrong rejection.

issues.title: vectorElemMinSize's classification cost grows with nesting depth squared
issues.verdictReason: At each of the N nesting levels, vectorElemMinSize calls isVectorVariableLengthType, which itself recurses down through the remaining depth to find the base type, giving O(N) work per level and O(N^2) total; the cost is bounded by the server-controlled type-string length so the practical impact is minimal, but the quadratic pattern is real and demonstrable by inspection of the recursion in marshal.go:1125-1145 and marshal.go:1181-1197.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize's recursion is new in this PR.
